PalletPoseStamped gains the chosen candidate's source index as the pallet sent through stage 2, and the source indices of the other class-matched candidates in that same Detection2DArray as deferred. findings: Faster R-CNN sends its second stage every proposal that survives proposal NMS. Ren, He, Girshick, and Sun fix that NMS at IoU 0.7, which leaves about 2000 regions per image; they train Fast R-CNN with 2000 RPN proposals and, for the VGG-16 system, test with 300 proposals per image (5 fps, 73.2% mAP on PASCAL VOC 2007). Regions outside that top set are discarded. The second stage scores the kept proposals, and the discarded regions are not written as deferred source indices on a pose result.

Cascade R-CNN adds three detection heads after the RPN, trained and run at IoU thresholds 0.5, 0.6, and 0.7. At inference the same cascade refines the surviving hypotheses, and outliers drop out as the threshold rises. Later heads still see the whole surviving set. A removed box is gone, rather than recorded as a deferred source index beside one chosen index on a pose message, and the later stage does not run once.

BYTE keeps almost every detection box and splits them at a score threshold tau, default 0.6. The first association matches the high-score set to Kalman tracks. The second association matches the low-score set to the tracks the first pass left unmatched, using IoU, and rejects a pair whose IoU is below 0.2. Unmatched low-score boxes are deleted as background. Unmatched high-score boxes start new tracks, and a lost track is kept for 30 frames. The deleted boxes are not a deferred index list on a pose result, and the low-score set gets a second association pass.

RT-DETR's uncertainty-minimal query selection initializes the decoder from the top 300 encoder features, using those features as content queries and their boxes as position queries. On COCO val2017 that selection raised the share of selected features with both classification and IoU scores above 0.5 from 0.30% to 0.67%, and AP from 47.9 to 48.7. Encoder features outside those 300 do not initialize a query. The decoder still runs on 300 queries, and the paper defines no deferred list of the unselected features on a pose result.

DenseFusion estimates a 6D pose for a set of known objects from one RGB-D frame. After semantic segmentation, the second stage runs for each segmented object on that mask's depth points, converted to a cloud, and on the RGB crop of the mask. Pixel-wise fusion then picks a pose by confidence, and iterative refinement repeats on that same object. Every segmented instance is posed. The other instances are further pose inputs, not deferred slots of one Detection2DArray carried on a single pose message.

GDR-Net regresses one object's 6D pose from one zoomed-in RGB RoI of 256 by 256. The network predicts dense correspondences, surface-region attention, and a visible mask at 64 by 64, and a convolutional Patch-PnP head reads those maps. Each detection is its own RoI. The other detections are additional RoIs, and the method uses no depth capture stamp and publishes no deferred source-index list on that pose.

CosyPose's first stage emits a 6D pose hypothesis for each detection in a view. The second stage matches those hypotheses across views, and the third stage refines cameras and objects by object-level bundle adjustment. The abstract states that the method does not require depth measurements. Other detections are posed and then matched. They are not left as deferred source indices on one pose that already carries this pair's RGB stamp and depth stamp.

vision_msgs/Detection2DArray is the list of proposals from one detector input. Detection2D.id is an optional string that should stay the same for one object across detection messages, and it may be empty. The message says the source image is not included and should be recovered with a time synchronizer. That id is a cross-message label. It is not the slot extract_detection_candidates stored, and the array is not a chosen index plus the other class-matched indices on the pose result.

REP-107 reports health on /diagnostics as a DiagnosticArray of DiagnosticStatus, default rate 1 Hz. Each status carries a level (OK, WARN, ERROR), a name, a message, a hardware_id, and a KeyValue list. That topic is the diagnostics stream. A roster that exists only there is on a channel the success-path pose consumer does not read, and the default rate is one hertz while the scene can still change.
